title: Rust: Error Handling
description: Handle errors with Result, Option, match, and the ? operator in Rust.

steps.title: Result Type Basics
steps.description: Write a function `safe_divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String>` that returns an error if b is 0. Call with (10, 2) and (10, 0).
hints: Use `match` to handle both cases when calling.

verification.failureMessage: Print Ok(5) for 10/2 and Error for 10/0.

steps.title: Using unwrap and expect
steps.description: Try parsing `"42"` and `"hello"` as integers using `"42".parse::<i32>()`. Use `.unwrap()` on the valid one and `.expect()` on the invalid one (catch the panic if needed).
hints: Use `std::panic::catch_unwind` to safely test the failure.

verification.failureMessage: Print 42 and catch the panic on invalid input.

steps.title: The ? Operator
steps.description: Write a function `parse_and_add(a: &str, b: &str) -> Result<i32, String>` that parses two strings and returns their sum, using `?` for error propagation.
hints: The `?` operator unwraps Ok or returns Err early.

verification.failureMessage: Print 30 for valid input and Error for invalid.

steps.title: Option Type
steps.description: Write a function `first_element<T>(vec: Vec<T>) -> Option<T>` that returns the first element of a Vec (or None if empty). Test with `[1, 2, 3]` and `[]`.
hints: Or use `if vec.is_empty() { None } else { Some(vec[0]) }`.
Print with match to handle both Some and None.

verification.failureMessage: Return Some(1) for [1,2,3] and None for [].

steps.title: Combined Error Handling
steps.description: Write a function `process_data(input: &str) -> Result<i32, String>` that: splits input by commas, parses each part, and returns the sum. Use `?` and handle all errors. Test with `"1,2,3"` and `"1,x,3"`.
